## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dove characterized by its slender body, soft gray-brown plumage, long pointed tail, small head, and dark spots on the wings. In Florida, it is common in open and semi-open habitats, including fields, agricultural areas, roadsides, pine flatwoods, scrub edges, parks, yards, and suburban landscapes. It feeds mainly on seeds, usually foraging on the ground in pairs or small flocks, and is often recognized by its soft mournful cooing and fast, whistling flight.
